title: Covering a Circle with Strips (Tarski's Plank Problem Intro)
full_prompt: Write a Manim script (compatible with ManimGL/Manim) that visualizes the concept of covering a unit circle with strips (planks) of varying widths. First, draw a circle of radius 2.5 with a radial line and a label '1' indicating its radius. Animate the circle's creation by rotating the radial line 360 degrees. Next, introduce a single teal strip across the circle. Use ValueTrackers to dynamically animate the strip's boundaries, showing its width shrinking and expanding using a dynamic DecimalNumber label that updates in real-time. Replace this decimal label with 'd_1'. Then, add three more colored strips (green, dark blue, light blue) with labels 'd_2', 'd_3', and 'd_4' at different angles and positions. After that, generate 10 random, semi-transparent strips covering the circle to represent a dense covering. Finally, transition the individual strip labels ('d_1', 'd_2', 'd_3', 'd_4') to the top of the screen to form a summation expression: 'd_1 + d_2 + d_3 + d_4 + ... + d_n'. Ensure smooth transitions, clean updaters, and proper layering so the circle and labels remain clearly visible.

common_failure_modes.note: The reference code relies on self.get_strip which is defined elsewhere in the module. The agent must implement a robust equivalent of get_strip or mock it using standard Manim shapes.
Using always_redraw or add_updater incorrectly can cause the width label to lag behind the strip's visual boundaries.
